census_method: exhaustive read of the central metrics registry (src/lighteval/metrics/metrics.py), the framework's own unit of scoring-logic reuse -- every task declares one of these 49 named metrics rather than implementing its own scoring, so this is a complete census, not a sample, despite the small population

VULNERABLE.exact_match: ExactMatches(strip_strings=True) -- raw string compare, no extraction step (this paper's EXACT_NO_EXTRACTION pattern)
VULNERABLE.expr_gold_metric: MultilingualExtractiveMatchMetric -- empty extraction list on failure
VULNERABLE.pass_at_k: PassAtK(strip_strings=True) -- default scoring, raw string compare
VULNERABLE.avg_at_n: AvgAtN(strip_strings=True) -- default scoring, raw string compare
VULNERABLE.maj_at_n: MajAtN() -- default scoring, raw string compare
VULNERABLE.g_pass_at_k: GPassAtK(strip_strings=True) -- default scoring, raw string compare
VULNERABLE.g_pass_at_k_latex: GPassAtK(sample_scoring_function=MultilingualExtractiveMatchMetric) -- boxed_match_priority=0, the same MATH-Hard boxed-answer pattern P2/E7 measure margins on

comparison_to_lm_eval_and_opencompass.note: Denominators are not the same unit: this counts METRICS in a registry, not TASK configurations -- one metric here typically backs dozens of tasks, so 12/37 vulnerable metrics almost certainly covers far more than 12/37 = 32.4% of lighteval's actual generative TASK count, but that per-task figure was not computed (the task registry was not audited; this census stops at the metric level, which is the framework's own true unit of scoring reuse). The qualitative finding -- silent coercion recurs in a third, architecturally different framework (centralized Python registry, not per-task YAML) from a third organisation -- is the load-bearing claim, not a fourth percentage to average against the other two.

shortest_complete_statement_of_the_failu.behaviour: returns [] (empty list, no exception, no distinct sentinel value) when no regex in the priority-ordered pattern set matches the prediction
shortest_complete_statement_of_the_failu.caller_code:
if all(len(p) == 0 for p in extracted_predictions):
    logger.warning(f"We did not manage to extract a prediction in the correct format...")
# ... falls through to:
return self.aggregation_function([
    1.0 if any(compare_gold_target(gold, pred, ...) for gold in extracted_golds) else 0.0
    for pred in extracted_predictions

shortest_complete_statement_of_the_failu.note: an empty extracted_predictions list makes `any(...)` over it vacuously False, so the item scores 0.0 -- identical to a genuinely wrong parsed answer. The warning goes to a Python logger, not to any field lighteval's own results JSON or leaderboard output reports.

notable.math_hard_relevance: pass_at_k_math, avg_at_n_math, g_pass_at_k_math and g_pass_at_k_latex all wrap MultilingualExtractiveMatchMetric with a boxed-answer LatexExtractionConfig -- the identical extraction target family this paper's own MATH-Hard leaderboard result (Sec. 6) uses margins for.
